subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept a new global `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` prompt-context configuration surface, and should no-override legacy subagent behavior remain outside the named `minimal` tier?
rationale: The patch changes a compatibility-sensitive config and session-context surface; automation can identify the mismatch, but maintainers must choose the public contract before the code and docs can be finalized.

options.title: Sponsor the tier contract
options.body: Keep the PR open, decide the intended legacy-vs-tier semantics, then require the branch to align resolver behavior, docs, and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Fold into broader context design
options.body: Pause this PR behind broader bootstrap/session filtering work so one maintainer-owned selector contract covers tiering and related context-pressure issues.

options.title: Decline the new config knob
options.body: Close this PR without merging and steer users toward existing contextInjection, bootstrap budgets, lightweight mode, or a narrower hook-filtering repair.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the tier contract
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, decide the intended legacy-vs-tier semantics, then require the branch to align resolver behavior, docs, and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame points to this owner on the central bootstrap filtering and resolver path, making them the best available product/compatibility decision owner.
